claims.text: Expected (mean) signed revenue loss for Pacific islands in 2026
Expected shortfall ES95 (positive-part tail shortfall) for Pacific islands in 2026

The two measures differ because they describe different parts of the loss distribution. The mean is a signed average over all simulated outcomes, retaining cases of revenue gain as well as loss, so gains offset losses. ES95 is a positive-part tail measure: it averages only the losses beyond the ninety-fifth percentile of the loss distribution, ignoring gains and near-average outcomes entirely. A right-skewed distribution with a modest central tendency but a fat adverse tail therefore shows an ES95 far above the mean.

For planning purposes the mean quantifies the expected central-case fiscal drag, while ES95 quantifies the size of severe-but-plausible outcomes in the worst tail, making it the more relevant figure for contingency buffers. The two figures should not be compared as if one were an error in the other; they answer different questions by construction.
